ideas: Staff feeling valued and more loyal
A small cost for a big boost in morale
Possible scheduling problems for small teams

phrases.meaning: balance between job and personal life
an extra benefit from a job
do someone's work while they're away

model: Yes, I definitely think companies should give staff a day off on their birthday. First, it's a small gesture, but it helps employees feel valued. For example, my company started offering a birthday day off last year. On my birthday, I was having breakfast with my parents instead of sitting in a meeting, and honestly, I felt really grateful to my manager. Something like that goes a long way, and it boosts morale much more than a free cake in the office. Another reason is that it supports work-life balance. Many people in Vietnam work long hours, and they rarely take leave. When my colleague took her birthday off, she spent the day with her young kids, and then she came back the next day full of energy. It's also a perk that costs the company very little, because colleagues can easily cover for each other for one day. So, in my view, this kind of policy really pays off, and more companies should try it.
